title.zh: 卷四百九十三 列傳第二百五十二 蠻夷一 西南溪峒諸蠻上
title.en: Volume 493 Biographies 252: Man People 1 - Man People from Xidong in the Southwest 1
title.raw: 卷四百九十三 列傳第二百五十二 蠻夷一 西南溪峒諸蠻上 Volume 493 Biographies 252: Man People 1 - Man People from Xidong in the Southwest 1

sentences.zh: 西南溪峒諸蠻上

translations.literal: The Various Man Peoples of the Southwestern Stream-Caves, Part One
translations.idiomatic: The Various Man Peoples of the Southwestern Stream-Caves, Part One

sentences.zh: 古者帝王之勤遠略，耀兵四裔，不過欲安內而捍外爾，非所以求逞也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when emperors and kings exerted themselves in far-reaching strategy and displayed their armies in the four borderlands, it was merely to secure the interior and defend against the exterior — not to seek to show off their prowess.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, sovereigns who labored over distant strategy and paraded their forces on every frontier did so only to calm the heartland and hold the outer realms at bay — not to gratify ambition for conquest.

sentences.zh: 西南諸蠻夷，重山復嶺，雜廁荊、楚、巴、黔、巫中，四面皆王土。

translations.literal: The various Man and Yi peoples of the southwest live amid layered mountains and overlapping ranges, intermixed among Jing, Chu, Ba, Qian, and Wu territories, with royal domain on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Man and Yi tribes of the southwest inhabit country of folded peaks and ridgelines, scattered through the lands of Jing, Chu, Ba, Qian, and Wu, yet bounded on every side by the king's domain.

sentences.zh: 乃欲揭上腴之征以取不毛之地，疲易使之眾而得梗化之氓，誠何益哉！

translations.literal: Yet to wish to levy heavy taxes on fertile lands in order to take barren ground, to wear out easily governed multitudes in order to gain stubborn and unassimilated subjects — what real benefit is there!
translations.idiomatic: To impose crushing levies on rich soil merely to annex worthless ground, or to exhaust a tractable population only to rule a people who resist assimilation — what could such a policy possibly gain?

sentences.zh: 樹其酋長，使自鎮撫，始終蠻夷遇之，斯計之得也。

translations.literal: To install their chieftains and let them pacify themselves, always treating them as Man and Yi — this is the successful policy.
translations.idiomatic: The sound approach is to recognize their chiefs and leave them to keep order among their own, treating them consistently as outer peoples rather than as ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 然無經久之策以控馭之，狌鼯之性便於跳梁，或以仇隙相尋，或以饑饉所逼，長嘯而起，出則衝突州縣，入則負固山林，致煩興師討捕，雖能殄除，而斯民之荼毒深矣。

translations.literal: Yet without a long-term policy to control and restrain them, their nature — like that of flying squirrels — is prone to leaping about; whether driven by vendettas or pressed by famine, they rise with a long cry. When they go out they clash with prefectures and counties; when they withdraw they hold fast in mountain forests. This forces the trouble of raising armies to hunt them down; though they can be exterminated, the suffering inflicted on the people is profound.
translations.idiomatic: Without enduring measures to hold them in check, their restless temperament — quick to bolt like a flying squirrel — sends them aloft at the slightest provocation, whether old feuds or hunger drive them. Out they surge against county seats; in they shelter among the hills. Campaign after campaign may crush them for a time, yet the common people pay a grievous price.

sentences.zh: 宋恃文教而略武衛，亦豈先王制荒服之道哉！

translations.literal: The Song relied on civil culture and education while neglecting military defense — how could this be the way of the former kings in governing the wild borderlands!
translations.idiomatic: The Song leaned on letters and ritual while slighting arms and garrisons — a far cry from the ancient kings' way of keeping the outer wilds in order.

sentences.zh: 西南溪峒諸蠻皆盤瓠種，唐虞為要服。

translations.literal: The various Man peoples of the southwestern stream-caves are all of the Panhu clan; under Yao and Shun they were in the yaofu zone of distant service.
translations.idiomatic: The Man tribes of the southwestern stream-caves trace descent to Panhu; in the age of Yao and Shun they already stood among the distant domains owing ritual duty.

sentences.zh: 周世，其眾彌盛，宣王命方叔伐之。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era their numbers grew ever greater, and King Xuan ordered Fang Shu to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou their population swelled until King Xuan sent Fang Shu against them.

sentences.zh: 楚莊既霸，遂服於楚。

translations.literal: After King Zhuang of Chu achieved hegemony, they thereupon submitted to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Once King Zhuang of Chu had made himself hegemon, they submitted to Chu.

sentences.zh: 秦昭使白起伐楚，略取蠻夷，置黔中郡，漢改為武陵。

translations.literal: King Zhao of Qin sent Bai Qi to attack Chu, seized the Man and Yi lands, and established Qianzhong Commandery; the Han renamed it Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Qin dispatched Bai Qi against Chu, took the Man and Yi territories, and set up Qianzhong Commandery, which the Han later renamed Wuling.

sentences.zh: 後漢建武中，大為寇鈔，遣伏波將軍馬援等至臨沅擊破之，渠帥饑困乞降。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Later Han they raided on a great scale; the court sent the Wave-Quelling General Ma Yuan and others to Lin-yuan, where they were defeated, and the chieftains, hungry and distressed, begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Han's Jianwu reign they harried the borders heavily until Ma Yuan, Wave-Quelling General, broke them at Lin-yuan; their leaders, starving and cornered, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 曆晉、宋、齊、梁、陳，或叛或服。

translations.literal: Through Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen they sometimes rebelled and sometimes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Jin, Liu-Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen dynasties they alternated between rebellion and submission.

sentences.zh: 隋置辰州，唐置錦州、溪州、巫州、敘州，皆其地也。

translations.literal: The Sui established Chen Prefecture; the Tang established Jin, Xi, Wu, and Xu prefectures — all within their territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui set up Chen Prefecture; the Tang added Jin, Xi, Wu, and Xu — all carved from their lands.

sentences.zh: 唐季之亂，蠻酋分據其地，自署為刺史。

translations.literal: In the turmoil at the end of Tang, Man chieftains divided and held their lands, appointing themselves prefects.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty collapsed into chaos, Man chiefs carved up the region and styled themselves prefects.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，馬希範承襲父業，據有湖南，時蠻徭保聚，依山阻江，殆十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Ma Xifan inherited his father's enterprise and held Hunan; at that time Man and Yao peoples gathered in fortified settlements along the mountains and blocked the rivers — nearly a hundred thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Jin's Tianfu reign Ma Xifan took over his father's domain in Hunan while Man and Yao groups, entrenched along rivers and ridges, numbered close to a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 至周行逢時，數出冠邊，逼辰、永二州，殺掠民畜無寧歲。

translations.literal: By the time of Zhou Xingfeng they repeatedly raided the borders, pressing Chen and Yong prefectures and slaughtering and plundering the people's livestock year after year without respite.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Xingfeng they harried the frontier again and again, threatening Chen and Yong and leaving the countryside without a single peaceful year.

sentences.zh: 太祖既下荊、湖，思得通蠻情、習險厄、勇智可任者以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had taken Jing and Hu, he sought someone who understood Man sentiments, was versed in difficult terrain, and possessed courage and wisdom fit for the task to pacify and govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu had secured Jing and the lake districts, he looked for a man who knew the Man peoples, understood the treacherous country, and had both nerve and wit enough to keep them quiet.

sentences.zh: 有辰州徭人秦再雄者，長七尺，武健多謀，在行逢時，屢以戰鬥立功，蠻黨伏之。

translations.literal: There was a Yao man of Chen Prefecture named Qin Zaixiong, seven feet tall, martial and resourceful; in Zhou Xingfeng's time he repeatedly won merit in battle, and the Man factions submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: A Yao warrior of Chen named Qin Zaixiong stood seven feet high — strong, shrewd, and repeatedly distinguished in Zhou Xingfeng's wars — and the Man clans looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 太祖召至闕下，察其可用，擢辰州刺史，官其子為殿直，賜予甚厚，仍使自辟吏屬，予一州租賦。

translations.literal: The Taizu summoned him to the capital, judged him usable, promoted him to Prefect of Chen, appointed his son as a Palace Duty Attendant, bestowed gifts in great abundance, and moreover allowed him to recruit his own staff and granted him one prefecture's tax revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu called him to court, found him fit for service, made him Prefect of Chen, gave his son a post in the palace guard, lavished rewards upon him, let him choose his own officials, and handed over the entire prefectural levy.

sentences.zh: 再雄感恩，誓死報效。

translations.literal: Zaixiong, moved by gratitude, vowed to repay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply grateful, Zaixiong pledged his life to the throne.

sentences.zh: 至州日訓練士兵，得三千人，皆能被甲渡水，曆山飛塹，捷如猿猱。

translations.literal: From the day he reached the prefecture he trained soldiers until he had three thousand men, all able to don armor, cross water, traverse mountains and leap ditches, swift as gibbons.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he drilled three thousand men who could march in armor, ford rivers, scale cliffs, and vault trenches with ape-like agility.

sentences.zh: 又選親校二十人分使諸蠻，以傳朝廷懷來之意，莫不從風而靡，各得降表以聞。

translations.literal: He also selected twenty trusted officers to dispatch among the various Man groups to convey the court's intent to win them over; none failed to bend before the wind, and each sent in a surrender memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: He sent twenty trusted officers among the tribes to carry the court's message of conciliation; one by one they bowed to the breeze, and memorials of submission reached the capital from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，復召至闕，面加獎激，改辰州團練使，又以其門客王允成為辰州推官。

translations.literal: The Taizu was greatly pleased, summoned him again to the capital, rewarded him face to face, changed his title to Training Commissioner of Chen, and also appointed his retainer Wang Yuncheng as Investigating Officer of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Taizu recalled him, praised him in person, made him Training Commissioner of Chen, and installed his client Wang Yuncheng as the prefecture's investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 再雄盡瘁邊圉，五州連袤數千里，不增一兵，不費帑庾，終太祖世，邊境無患。

translations.literal: Zaixiong exhausted himself on the border; five prefectures stretched in unbroken extent for several thousand li — he added not a single soldier and spent not from the state granaries, yet through Taizu's entire reign the frontier knew no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixiong gave his all along a thousand-mile belt of five prefectures without asking for more troops or treasury grain, and through Taizu's lifetime the border stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 又有溪州刺史彭士愁等以溪、錦、獎州歸馬氏，立銅柱為界。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prefect of Xi Peng Shichou and others submitted Xi, Jin, and Jiang prefectures to the Ma clan and erected a bronze pillar as a boundary marker.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi Prefect Peng Shichou and others had yielded Xi, Jin, and Jiang to the Ma house and set up a bronze pillar to mark the border.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，知溪州彭允林、前溪州刺史田洪贇等列狀歸順，詔以允林為溪州刺史，洪贇為萬州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, the acting Prefect of Xi Peng Yunlin, the former Prefect of Xi Tian Hongyun, and others submitted memorials of submission; an edict appointed Yunlin Prefect of Xi and Hongyun Prefect of Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4 Peng Yunlin, acting prefect of Xi, Tian Hongyun, former prefect of Xi, and others petitioned to submit; the throne named Yunlin prefect of Xi and Hongyun prefect of Wan.

sentences.zh: 允林卒，以其子師皎代為刺史。

translations.literal: When Yunlin died, his son Shijiao was appointed prefect in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunlin's death his son Shijiao succeeded him as prefect.

sentences.zh: 四月，水鬥都虞候林抱義上辰、敘二州圖。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Lin Baoyi, Chief Assistant of the Water-Fighting Corps, presented maps of Chen and Xu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Lin Baoyi of the Water-Fighting command submitted maps of Chen and Xu.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年四月，溪、敘、獎等州民相攻劫，遣殿直牛允齎詔諭之，乃定。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Qiande, the peoples of Xi, Xu, Jiang, and other prefectures attacked and plundered one another; the court sent Palace Duty Attendant Niu Yun bearing an edict to instruct them, and order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 2/4 the tribes of Xi, Xu, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures fell to raiding one another until Niu Yun arrived with an imperial instruction and peace returned.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，珍州刺史田景遷內附。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, Tian Jingqian, Prefect of Zhen, submitted to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year three Zhen Prefect Tian Jingqian came in from the hills.

sentences.zh: 五溪團練使、洽州刺史田處崇上言：「湖南節度馬希範建敘州潭陽縣為懿州，署臣叔父萬盈為刺史。

translations.literal: Tian Chuchong, Training Commissioner of the Five Streams and Prefect of Qia, memorialized: "The Hunan Military Commissioner Ma Xifan elevated Tan-yang County of Xu Prefecture to Yi Prefecture and appointed my uncle Wanying as prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chuchong, commissioner of the Five Streams and prefect of Qia, wrote: "When Ma Xifan ruled Hunan he raised Tan-yang in Xu to Yi Prefecture and made my uncle Wanying its prefect."

sentences.zh: 希範卒，其弟希萼襲位，改為洽州，願復舊名。

translations.literal: When Xifan died his younger brother Xie succeeded and changed it to Qia Prefecture; we wish to restore the former name."
translations.idiomatic: After Xifan's death his brother Xie took power and renamed it Qia; we ask that the old name be restored."

sentences.zh: 」詔從其請。

translations.literal: An edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the request.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔溪州宜充五溪團練使，刻印以賜之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict directed that Xi Prefecture should serve as Training Commissioner of the Five Streams, and a seal was carved and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xi was ordered to head the Five Streams command, and a seal was cut and granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，南州進銅鼓內附，下溪州刺史田思遷亦以銅鼓、虎皮、麝臍來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Nan Prefecture presented a bronze drum in submission; Tian Siqian, Prefect of Lower Xi, also came to offer tribute of bronze drums, tiger skins, and musk pods.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Nan Prefecture sent in a bronze drum as a token of allegiance, and Lower Xi Prefect Tian Siqian brought drums, tiger pelts, and musk navel sacs as tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，以溪州團練使彭允足為濮州牢城都指揮使，溪州義軍都指揮使彭允賢為衛州牢城都指揮使，珍州錄事參軍田思曉為博州牢城都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year, Peng Yunzu, Training Commissioner of Xi, was made Commander-in-Chief of the Prison City at Pu; Peng Yunxian, Commander-in-Chief of the Xi Loyal Army, was made Commander-in-Chief of the Prison City at Wei; and Tian Sixiao, Registrar of Zhen, was made Commander-in-Chief of the Prison City at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Peng Yunzu of Xi was posted to command Pu's prison garrison, Peng Yunxian of the Xi loyal forces to Wei's, and Zhen registrar Tian Sixiao to Bo's.

sentences.zh: 允足等溪峒酋豪據山險，持兩端，故因其入朝而置之內地。

translations.literal: Yunzu and the other stream-cave chieftains held mountain strongholds and kept to both sides; therefore, when they came to court they were stationed in the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yunzu were hill chiefs who hedged their bets; the court used their audience visits to resettle them inland.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年，珍州刺史田景遷言，本州連歲災沴，乞改為高州，從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaibao, Tian Jingqian, Prefect of Zhen, stated that the prefecture had suffered disasters year after year and begged that it be renamed Gao Prefecture; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 1 Zhen Prefect Tian Jingqian reported repeated calamities and asked that the name be changed to Gao; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，景遷卒，其子衙內都指揮使彥伊來請命，即以為刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jingqian died; his son Yanyi, Commander-in-Chief of the Inner Yamen, came to request appointment and was immediately made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Jingqian died; his son Yanyi, commander of the inner guard, sought the post and was named prefect at once.

sentences.zh: 九年，獎州刺史田處達以丹砂、石英來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Tian Chuda, Prefect of Jiang, came to offer tribute of cinnabar and quartz.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine Jiang Prefect Tian Chuda presented cinnabar and quartz as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，懿州刺史、五溪都團練使田漢瓊以其子、弟、女夫、大將、五溪統軍都指揮使田漢度而下十二人來貢，詔並加檢校官以獎之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Tian Hanqiong, Prefect of Yi and Overall Training Commissioner of the Five Streams, came to offer tribute with his son, younger brother, son-in-law, great general, Tian Handu — Commander-in-Chief of the Five Streams armies — and eleven others below them; an edict added honorary inspector ranks to all as reward.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 Yi Prefect and Five Streams commissioner Tian Hanqiong arrived with twelve kin and officers, including his son, brother, son-in-law, and army commander Tian Handu; the court rewarded them all with honorary inspector titles.

sentences.zh: 三年，夷州蠻任朗政等來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, Ren Langzheng of the Yi Prefecture Man and others came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Ren Langzheng of Yi and other Man leaders brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔辰州不得移部內馬氏所鑄銅柱。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict forbade Chen Prefecture to move the bronze pillar cast by the Ma clan within its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Chen was ordered not to relocate the Ma house's bronze boundary pillar within the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 溪州刺史彭允殊上言：「刺史舊三年則為州所易，望朝廷禁止。

translations.literal: Peng Yunshu, Prefect of Xi, memorialized: "By old custom the prefect is replaced every three years by the prefecture; we hope the court will forbid this."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Prefect Peng Yunshu wrote: "Custom has the prefect turned out every three years; we ask the throne to end the practice."

sentences.zh: 」賜敕書安撫之。

translations.literal: A rescript of reassurance was bestowed to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a reassuring edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 八年，錦、溪、敘、富四州蠻相率詣辰州，言願比內郡輸租稅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Man of Jin, Xi, Xu, and Fu prefectures came in groups to Chen Prefecture, stating that they wished to pay land tax like interior commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Man leaders from Jin, Xi, Xu, and Fu flocked to Chen and asked to pay regular taxes like interior counties.

sentences.zh: 詔長吏察其謠俗情偽，並按視山川地形圖畫來上，卒不許。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief officials to investigate their customs and true sentiments, survey the mountains and rivers, and submit maps — yet in the end permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were told to study their customs, survey the terrain, and send maps — but the request was ultimately denied.

sentences.zh: 懿州刺史田漢瓊、錦州刺史田漢希上言，願兩易其地，詔從之。

translations.literal: Tian Hanqiong, Prefect of Yi, and Tian Hanxi, Prefect of Jin, memorialized that they wished to exchange their territories; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Prefect Tian Hanqiong and Jin Prefect Tian Hanxi asked to swap domains; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 又以知敘州舒德郛為刺史。

translations.literal: Shu Defu, acting Prefect of Xu, was also appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Defu, who had been acting prefect of Xu, was confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，黔南言溪峒夷獠疾病，擊銅鼓、沙鑼以祀神鬼，詔釋其銅禁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, Qiannan reported that the stream-cave Yi and Liao were afflicted with illness and struck bronze drums and sand gongs to worship spirits; an edict lifted the ban on copper for them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 1 the south of Qian reported that stream-cave tribes, stricken with disease, beat bronze drums and gongs for the spirits; the court exempted them from the copper prohibition.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，知晃州田漢權言，本管砂井步夷人粟忠獲古晃州印一鈕來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, Tian Hanquan, acting Prefect of Huang, reported that the Yi man Su Zhong of Shajingbu in his jurisdiction had obtained and presented one knob of an ancient Huang Prefecture seal.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 acting Huang Prefect Tian Hanquan reported that Su Zhong, a Yi tribesman of Shajingbu, had found and presented a knob from an old Huang seal.

sentences.zh: 因請命以漢權為晃州刺史。

translations.literal: He therefore requested appointment of Hanquan as Prefect of Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Hanquan be named prefect of Huang.

sentences.zh: 又以五溪諸州統軍、鶴州刺史向通漢為富州刺史，從其請也。

translations.literal: Xiang Tonghan, Overall Commander of the Five Streams prefectures and Prefect of He, was also made Prefect of Fu — his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Tonghan, commander of the Five Streams and prefect of He, was given Fu as well, as he had asked.

sentences.zh: 是年，荊湖轉運使言，富州向萬通殺皮師勝父子七人，取五藏及首以祀魔鬼。

translations.literal: That year the Jing-Hu Transport Commissioner reported that Xiang Wantong of Fu had killed seven persons of the Pi Shisheng father-and-son household, taken their viscera and heads to worship demons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Jing-Hu transport commissioner reported that Fu's Xiang Wantong had slain seven members of the Pi Shisheng family and offered their organs and heads to evil spirits.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其遠俗，令勿問。

translations.literal: The court, considering their distant customs, ordered that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Because theirs were remote customs, the court declined to investigate.

sentences.zh: 三年，晁州刺史田漢權、錦州刺史田保全遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, Tian Hanquan, Prefect of Chao, and Tian Baoquan, Prefect of Jin, dispatched envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Chao Prefect Tian Hanquan and Jin Prefect Tian Baoquan sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，以舒德言為元州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Shu Deyan was made Prefect of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Shu Deyan was appointed prefect of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 獎、晃、敘、懿、元、錦、費、福等州皆來貢，上親視器幣以賜之。

translations.literal: Jiang, Huang, Xu, Yi, Yuan, Jin, Fei, Fu, and other prefectures all came to offer tribute; the emperor personally inspected the vessels and gifts before bestowing rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, Huang, Xu, Yi, Yuan, Jin, Fei, Fu, and the rest all sent tribute; the emperor himself examined the gifts before granting return presents.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，高州、溪州並來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, Gao and Xi prefectures both came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 Gao and Xi both presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年，上親祀南郊，富州刺史向通漢上言：「聖人郊祀，恩浹天壤，況五溪諸州連接十洞，控西南夷戎之地。

translations.literal: In the second year the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Altar; Xiang Tonghan, Prefect of Fu, memorialized: "When the sage performs suburban sacrifice, his grace saturates heaven and earth — how much more so for the Five Streams prefectures, which connect the Ten Caves and guard the lands of the southwestern Yi and Rong!"
translations.idiomatic: In year two the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar in person; Fu Prefect Xiang Tonghan wrote: "When the Son of Heaven worships at the suburbs, his grace floods heaven and earth — and all the more for the Five Streams, which link the Ten Caves and stand guard over the Yi and Rong of the southwest."

sentences.zh: 惟臣州自昔至今，為辰州牆壁，障護辰州五邑，王民安居。

translations.literal: My prefecture alone, from past to present, has been the wall of Chen Prefecture, shielding its five districts so that the king's people may dwell in peace.
translations.idiomatic: My prefecture alone has long been Chen's rampart, sheltering its five districts so the emperor's subjects could live untroubled.

sentences.zh: 臣雖僻處遐荒，洗心事上，伏望陛下察臣勤王之誠，因茲郊禮，特加真命。

translations.literal: Though I dwell in remote wilds, I purify my heart in service to the throne; I humbly hope Your Majesty will perceive my loyalty to the king and, on account of this suburban rite, grant a special true appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Though I live at the edge of the world, my heart is clean in your service; I beg Your Majesty to see my loyalty and, on this sacred occasion, bestow a formal commission.

sentences.zh: 」詔加通漢檢校司徒，進封河內郡侯。

translations.literal: An edict added to Tonghan the honorary rank of Minister of Education and advanced him to Marquis of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Tonghan honorary Minister of Education and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Henei.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，天賜州蠻向永豐等二十九人來朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, twenty-nine Man of Tianci Prefecture including Xiang Yongfeng came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year five twenty-nine men of Tianci, led by Xiang Yongfeng, presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 夔州路轉運使丁謂言：「溪蠻入粟實緣邊砦柵，頓息施、萬諸州饋餉之弊。

translations.literal: Ding Wei, Transport Commissioner of the Kuizhou Circuit, stated: "The stream Man bringing in grain truly supplies the border stockades and forts, and at once relieves the trouble of provisioning Shi and Wan prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhou transport commissioner Ding Wei reported: "Grain from the stream Man now fills our border forts and has ended the costly relay of supplies through Shi and Wan."

sentences.zh: 臣觀自昔和戎安邊，未有境外轉糧給我戍兵者。

translations.literal: In my view, from antiquity in pacifying the Rong and securing the border, there has never been a case of peoples beyond the frontier transporting grain to supply our garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Never before, in all the history of appeasing frontier peoples, had outsiders shipped grain to feed our garrisons.

sentences.zh: 」先是，蠻人數擾，上召問巡檢使侯廷賞，廷賞曰：「蠻無他求，唯欲鹽爾。

translations.literal: Earlier the Man had repeatedly harassed the border; the emperor summoned and questioned Patrol Commissioner Hou Tingshang, who said: "The Man have no other demand — they only want salt."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Man had raided repeatedly, the emperor asked patrol commissioner Hou Tingshang, who answered: "They want nothing else — only salt."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此常人所欲，何不與之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is what ordinary people desire — why not give it to them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is what anyone would want — why withhold it?"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔諭丁謂，謂即傳告陬落，群蠻感悅，因相與盟約，不為寇鈔，負約者，眾殺之。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to instruct Ding Wei; Wei at once conveyed the message to the hamlets, and the Man tribes were moved with joy. They therefore made a covenant among themselves not to raid; whoever broke the covenant, the multitude would kill.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to Ding Wei, who spread the word through the hamlets; the tribes rejoiced, swore not to raid, and agreed that anyone who broke faith would be put to death by the community.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「天子濟我以食鹽，我願輸與兵食。

translations.literal: They also said: "The Son of Heaven has aided us with edible salt; we wish to deliver grain for the troops."
translations.idiomatic: They declared: "The emperor has given us salt; we will supply grain for the army."

sentences.zh: 」 自是邊穀有三年之積。

translations.literal: From then on the border granaries held a three-year store.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the frontier stores held three years' grain.

sentences.zh: 七月，高州刺史田彥伊子承寶等百二十二人來朝，賜巾服、器幣，以承寶為山河使、九溪十峒撫諭都監。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Tian Yanyi of Gao and his son Chengbao and one hundred twenty others came to court; headcloths, robes, vessels, and gifts were bestowed, and Chengbao was made River-and-Mountain Envoy and Overall Supervisor of Pacification for the Nine Streams and Ten Caves.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gao Prefect Tian Yanyi's son Chengbao led 122 men to court; they received caps, robes, and gifts, and Chengbao was named River-and-Mountain envoy and chief pacifier of the Nine Streams and Ten Caves.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，丁謂等言，高州義軍務頭角田承進等擒生蠻六百六十餘人，奪所略漢口四百餘人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, Ding Wei and others reported that Tian Chengjin and others of the Gao Loyal Army's service corps had captured more than six hundred and sixty living Man and recovered more than four hundred Han people they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year six Ding Wei reported that Tian Chengjin of Gao's loyal forces had taken over 660 captive Man and freed more than 400 Han subjects they had carried off.

sentences.zh: 初，益州軍亂，議者恐緣江下峽，乃集施、黔、高、溪蠻豪子弟捍禦，群蠻因熟漢路，寇略而歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Yizhou army mutinied, advisers feared they might come down the river through the gorges; Man chieftains' sons and younger brothers from Shi, Qian, Gao, and Xi were gathered to defend, but the Man tribes, having learned the Han routes, raided and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yizhou garrison mutinied, courtiers feared a descent through the gorges and called up sons of Man chiefs from Shi, Qian, Gao, and Xi to guard the passes — but the tribes, now knowing the Han roads, raided and slipped home.

sentences.zh: 謂等至，即召與盟，令還漢口。

translations.literal: When Wei and the others arrived, they were summoned to covenant at once and ordered to return the Han captives.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei arrived he summoned them to swear peace and ordered the Han captives released.

sentences.zh: 既而有生蠻違約，謂遣承進率眾及發州兵擒獲之，焚其室廬，皆震懾伏罪。

translations.literal: Afterward some living Man broke the covenant; Wei sent Chengjin leading his forces together with dispatched prefectural troops to capture them, burned their dwellings, and all were awed into confessing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When some Man broke faith, Wei sent Chengjin with local troops to seize them, burn their villages, and cow them into submission.

sentences.zh: 謂乃置尖木砦施州界，以控扼之，自是寇鈔始息，邊溪峒田民得耕種。

translations.literal: Wei then established the Sharp-Wood Stockade on the Shi Prefecture border to control and restrain them; from then raiding began to cease, and the farming people of the border stream-caves could cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei built Sharp-Wood stockade on the Shi border to choke the passes; raids dwindled, and farmers in the stream-caves could till their fields again.

sentences.zh: 七月，南高州義軍指揮使田彥強、防虞指揮使田承海來貢，施州叛蠻譚仲通等三十餘人來歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Tian Yanqiang, Commander of the Southern Gao Loyal Army, and Tian Chenghai, Commander of Frontier Defense, came to offer tribute; more than thirty rebellious Man of Shi including Tan Zhongtong came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gao commanders Tian Yanqiang and Tian Chenghai brought tribute, while over thirty Shi rebels led by Tan Zhongtong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，高州五姓義軍指揮使田文鄯來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, Tian Wenshan, Commander of the Gao Five-Clan Loyal Army, came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 1 Tian Wenshan, commander of Gao's Five-Clan loyal army, presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 富州刺史向通漢遣使潭州營佛事，以報朝廷存恤之惠。

translations.literal: Xiang Tonghan, Prefect of Fu, dispatched envoys to Tanzhou to perform Buddhist rites in return for the court's gracious care.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Prefect Xiang Tonghan sent men to Tanzhou to sponsor Buddhist services in thanks for the court's kindness.

sentences.zh: 二年，夔州路降蠻首領皆自署職名，請因而命之，上不許，第令次補牙校。

translations.literal: In the second year, surrendered Man chieftains of the Kuizhou Circuit all styled themselves with office titles and asked to be appointed accordingly; the emperor did not permit it, ordering only that they be registered as deputy commanders in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In year two surrendered Kuizhou chiefs had taken titles for themselves and asked for recognition; the emperor refused and told them to queue for deputy-commander posts instead.

sentences.zh: 是歲，辰州諸蠻攻下溪州，為其刺史彭儒猛擊走之，擒酋首以獻，詔賜儒猛錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: That year the various Man of Chen attacked Lower Xi Prefecture; Peng Rumeng, its prefect, drove them off, captured chieftains and presented them; an edict bestowed on Rumeng a brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chen Man raided Lower Xi; prefect Peng Rumeng repulsed them, sent captured chiefs to court, and received a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 儒猛自陳母老，願被恩典，詔特加邑封。

translations.literal: Rumeng himself stated that his mother was aged and wished to receive grace; an edict specially added a fief seal for her.
translations.idiomatic: Rumeng pleaded that his mother was elderly and deserved favor; the court granted her a special enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 十二月，荊湖北路言，溪峒團練使彭文綰送還先陷漢口五十人，詔授文綰檢校太子賓客，知中彭州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Jinghu North Circuit reported that Peng Wenwan, Training Commissioner of the stream-caves, had returned fifty Han captives previously seized; an edict appointed Wenwan Honorary Guest of the Heir Apparent and acting Prefect of Zhong Peng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jinghu North reported that stream-cave commissioner Peng Wenwan had freed fifty Han captives; he was made honorary guest of the heir apparent and acting prefect of Zhong Peng.

sentences.zh: 其年，懿州刺史田漢希卒，以其子漢能為刺史。

translations.literal: That year Tian Hanxi, Prefect of Yi, died, and his son Hanneng was made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yi Prefect Tian Hanxi died and his son Hanneng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 三年，高州新附蠻酋八十九人來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, eighty-nine newly submitted Man chieftains of Gao came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year three eighty-nine newly submitted Gao chiefs brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 五溪都防禦使向通漢表求追贈父母，從之。

translations.literal: Xiang Tonghan, Overall Defense Commissioner of the Five Streams, memorialized requesting posthumous honors for his parents; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Five Streams defense commissioner Xiang Tonghan asked posthumous titles for his parents; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 溪州刺史彭文慶率溪峒群蠻來朝。

translations.literal: Peng Wenqing, Prefect of Xi, led the stream-cave Man tribes to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Prefect Peng Wenqing led the stream-cave tribes to court.

sentences.zh: 又高州諸名豪百餘人入貢。

translations.literal: Moreover, more than a hundred notable leaders of Gao came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred Gao notables also presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，以高州刺史田彥伊子承寶為寧武郎將，高州土軍都指揮使田思欽為安化郎將。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, Chengbao, son of Tian Yanyi of Gao, was made General of Tranquil Martiality; Tian Siqin, Commander-in-Chief of the Gao Native Army, was made General of Pacifying Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year four Yanyi's son Chengbao was named General of Tranquil Martiality and native-army commander Tian Siqin General of Pacifying Transformation.

sentences.zh: 其年，宜州軍亂，朝廷恐宜、融溪峒因緣侵擾，因降詔約勒首領，皆奉詔，部分種族，無敢輒動。

translations.literal: That year the Yizhou army mutinied; the court feared the Yi and Rong stream-caves might take advantage to harass, and therefore issued an edict to bind the chieftains — all obeyed the edict, apportioned their clans, and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: That year troops mutinied at Yizhou; fearing stream-cave raids from Yi and Rong, the court sent restraining edicts — every chief obeyed, kept his people in line, and none stirred.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，夔州路言，五團蠻嘯聚，謀劫高州，欲令暗利砦援之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the Kuizhou Circuit reported that the Five-Tuan Man had gathered with war cries, plotting to raid Gao Prefecture and wishing to have Anli Stockade come to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 1 Kuizhou reported that Five-Tuan Man had massed, planning to strike Gao with help from Anli stockade.

sentences.zh: 上以蠻夷自相攻，不許發兵。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that the Man and Yi were attacking one another, did not permit troops to be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that they were fighting among themselves and refused to send troops.

sentences.zh: 三月，知元州舒君強、知古州向光普並加銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the third month, Shu Junqiang, acting Prefect of Yuan, and Xiang Guangpu, acting Prefect of Gu, were both given the Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month acting Yuan prefect Shu Junqiang and acting Gu prefect Xiang Guangpu were both made Silver-Gleam grand masters and honorary guests of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 八月，黔州言，磨嵯、洛浦蠻首領龔行滿等率族二千三百人歸順。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Qian Prefecture reported that Gong Xingman and other chieftains of the Mocuo and Luopu Man led two thousand three hundred clansmen to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Qian reported that Mocuo and Luopu chiefs led by Gong Xingman brought 2,300 clansmen to submit.

sentences.zh: 十月，溪峒諸蠻獻方物於泰山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the various stream-cave Man presented local products at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month stream-cave tribes presented local tribute at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 三年，澧州言，慈利縣蠻相仇劫，知州劉仁霸請率兵定之。

translations.literal: In the third year Li Prefecture reported that the Man of Cili County were feuding and plundering one another; Prefect Liu Renba requested to lead troops to settle it.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Li reported Man feuds and raids in Cili; prefect Liu Renba asked to march troops to restore order.

sentences.zh: 上恐深入蠻境，使其疑懼，止令仁霸宣諭詔旨，遂皆感服。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that penetrating deep into Man territory would make them suspicious and afraid; he ordered only that Renba proclaim the edict, and all were moved to submission.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that an invasion would only alarm them, the emperor told Renba to announce the edict instead — and the tribes submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 四年，安、遠、順、南、永寧、濁水州蠻酋田承曉等三百七十三人來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Tian Chengxiiao and three hundred seventy-two other Man chieftains of An, Yuan, Shun, Nan, Yongning, and Zhuoshui prefectures came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Tian Chengxiiao and 372 other chiefs from An, Yuan, Shun, Nan, Yongning, and Zhuoshui presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔：「昨許溪峒蠻夷歸先劫漢口及五十人者，特署職名，仍聽來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict stated: "Yesterday permission was granted to the stream-cave Man and Yi who returned those previously seized at Hankou and the fifty persons — they are specially granted official titles and still permitted to come with tribute."
translations.idiomatic: In year five the throne proclaimed: "Those stream-cave tribes who yesterday restored the Hankou captives and the fifty men they had taken shall receive special appointments and may continue to present tribute."

sentences.zh: 如聞緣此要利，輒掠邊民充數，所在切辨察之。

translations.literal: If it is heard that because of this they seek profit and promptly plunder frontier people to pad the numbers, everywhere strictly distinguish and investigate this.
translations.idiomatic: "Should anyone pad the rolls by raiding border villagers for profit, local officials must investigate each case rigorously."

sentences.zh: 」其年，夔蠻千五百人乞朝貢，上慮其勞費，不許。

translations.literal: " That year, fifteen hundred Kuai Man begged to come to court with tribute; the emperor feared the labor and expense and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: That same year fifteen hundred Kuai tribesmen asked leave to attend court; fearing the cost, the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又詔：施州溪蠻朔望犒以酒肴。

translations.literal: Another edict: the stream-cave Man of Shizhou were to be rewarded with wine and food on the new and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: Another order directed that Shi stream-cave tribes receive wine and viands on each new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 閏十月，五溪蠻向貴升及磨嵯、洛浦蠻來貢。

translations.literal: In the intercalary tenth month, the Five Streams Man Xiang Guisheng and the Mo Cuo and Luopu Man came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month Five Streams chief Xiang Guisheng came to court, along with Man from Mo Cuo and Luopu.

sentences.zh: 六年，夔州蠻彭延暹、龔才晃等來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Kuizhou Man Peng Yanxian, Gong Caihuang, and others came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Kuizhou chiefs Peng Yanxian and Gong Caihuang presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 辰州溪峒都指揮使魏進武率山徭數百人數寇城砦，朝廷不欲發兵窮討，乃降詔招諭。

translations.literal: Wei Jinwu, Overall Commander of the Chenzhou stream-caves, led several hundred mountain Yao on repeated raids against fortified towns; the court did not wish to send troops for a thorough punitive campaign and therefore issued an edict to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen stream-cave commander Wei Jinwu led hundreds of mountain Yao in repeated assaults on border forts; unwilling to mount a full expedition, the court sent edicts summoning him to terms.

sentences.zh: 七年，進武詣吏請罪，署為三班借職，監房州稅，仍賜裝錢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Jinwu went to officials to plead guilty; he was appointed Acting Third-Rank Attendant, supervising taxes at Fangzhou, and travel funds were also bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Jinwu surrendered and pleaded guilty; he received an acting third-rank post supervising Fangzhou taxes, plus outfit money.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔中彭州彭文綰歲賜錦袍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict granted Peng Wenwan of Zhong Peng an annual gift of a brocade robe.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Wenwan of Zhong Peng was granted a brocade robe every year.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，溪州蠻寇擾，遣兵討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, Xi Prefecture Man raided and harassed; troops were dispatched to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi 1 brought Xi Man raids; the court sent troops against them.

sentences.zh: 二年，辰州都巡檢使李守元率兵入白霧團，擒蠻寇十五人，斬首百級，降其酋二百餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year, Li Shouyuan, Overall Patrol Commissioner of Chenzhou, led troops into the Baiwu regiment, captured fifteen Man raiders, beheaded one hundred heads, and induced more than two hundred of their chiefs to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In year two Chen patrol commander Li Shouyuan entered Baiwu district, took fifteen raiders, claimed a hundred heads, and brought in over two hundred chiefs.

sentences.zh: 知辰州錢絳等入下溪州，破砦柵，斬蠻六十餘人，降老幼千餘。

translations.literal: Qian Jiang, Administrator of Chenzhou, and others entered Lower Xi Prefecture, stormed stockades and palisades, beheaded more than sixty Man, and induced more than a thousand old and young to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Chen prefect Qian Jiang pushed into Lower Xi, overran their forts, killed sixty-odd fighters, and accepted the surrender of a thousand old and young.

sentences.zh: 刺史彭儒猛亡入山林，執其子仕漢等赴闕。

translations.literal: Prefect Peng Rumeng fled into the mountain forests; his sons Shihan and others were seized and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Peng Rumeng vanished into the hills; his son Shihan and others were seized and sent to court.

sentences.zh: 詔高州蠻，捕儒猛來獻者厚加賞典。

translations.literal: An edict to the Gao Man: whoever captured Rumeng and presented him would receive lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Gao tribes were promised rich rewards for anyone who captured Rumeng and delivered him to court.

sentences.zh: 其年，儒猛因順州蠻田彥晏上狀本路，自訴求歸。

translations.literal: That year, Rumeng, through Shun Prefecture Man Tian Yanyan, submitted a report to the circuit, pleading on his own behalf to return.
translations.idiomatic: That year Rumeng petitioned through Shun chief Tian Yanyan, asking leave to come home.

sentences.zh: 轉運使以聞，上哀憐之，特許釋罪。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported it; the emperor pitied him and specially permitted release from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the transport commissioner relayed the plea, the emperor pitied him and granted amnesty.

sentences.zh: 儒猛乃奉上所略民口、器甲，詔辰州通判劉中象召至明灘，與歃血要盟，遣之。

translations.literal: Rumeng then presented the people and armor he had seized; an edict ordered Chen Vice-Prefect Liu Zhongxiang to summon him to Mingtan, swear a blood-oath covenant with him, and send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Rumeng restored captives and weapons; vice-prefect Liu Zhongxiang was ordered to meet him at Mingtan for a blood covenant, then send him home.

sentences.zh: 詔以仕漢為殿直，儒霸、儒聰為借職，賜冠帶、緡帛。

translations.literal: An edict made Shihan a Palace Attendant, Rubba and Rucong Acting Attendants, and bestowed caps, belts, and silk cash.
translations.idiomatic: Shihan was made palace attendant; Rubba and Rucong received acting ranks, caps, belts, and silks.

sentences.zh: 富州刺史向通漢率所部來朝，貢名馬、丹砂、銀裝劍槊、兜鍪、彩牌等物。

translations.literal: Xiang Tonghan, Prefect of Fu, led his following to court, presenting famed horses, cinnabar, silver-mounted swords and spears, helmets, painted shields, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Prefect Xiang Tonghan brought his people to court with famed horses, cinnabar, silver-trimmed arms, helmets, painted shields, and more.

sentences.zh: 詔賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬，並其子光澤以下器幣有差，特許通漢五日一朝。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed ceremonial robes, gold belt, and saddled horse; his son Guangze and those below received utensils and silks in graded amounts; Tonghan was specially permitted to attend court every five days.
translations.idiomatic: He received court robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse; sons including Guangze got graded gifts; Tonghan alone was allowed to attend every five days.

sentences.zh: 逾月，通漢上《五溪地理圖》，願留京師，上嘉美之，特授通漢檢校太傅、本州防禦使，還賜疆土，署其子光澤等三班職名。

translations.literal: After a month Tonghan submitted a "Geographic Map of the Five Streams," wishing to remain in the capital; the emperor praised this and specially appointed Tonghan Honorary Grand Mentor and Defense Commissioner of his prefecture, restored his domain, and registered his son Guangze and others for Third-Rank offices.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he presented a map of the Five Streams and asked to stay in the capital; delighted, the throne made him honorary grand mentor and defense commissioner, restored his lands, and registered Guangze for third-rank posts.

sentences.zh: 通漢再表欲留京師，不允，乃為光澤等求內地監臨，及言歲賜衣，願使者至本任，並從之。

translations.literal: Tonghan again memorialized wishing to remain in the capital; this was not granted. He then sought inland supervisory posts for Guangze and others, and stated that for the annual gift of robes he wished envoys to come to his post — all was granted.
translations.idiomatic: A second plea to remain was denied; he then secured inland posts for his sons and asked that yearly robes be delivered to his seat — all granted.

sentences.zh: 既辭，又賜以襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: When he took leave, he was again bestowed ceremonial robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure he received robes and a gold belt again.

sentences.zh: 三年，通漢卒，以其子光憲知州事。

translations.literal: In the third year, Tonghan died; his son Guangxian was put in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Tonghan died; his son Guangxian took over the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其後，光澤不為親族所容，上表納土，上察其意，不許。

translations.literal: Thereafter Guangze was not tolerated by his kin; he memorialized offering his lands to the state; the emperor perceived his intent and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guangze, shunned by his clan, offered to surrender his territory; the court read his motive and refused.

sentences.zh: 四年，知古州向光普遣使鼎州營僧齋，以祝聖壽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Xiang Guangpu, Administrator of Gu, dispatched envoys to Dingzhou to sponsor a monastic feast in prayer for the sage's longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Gu prefect Xiang Guangpu sent men to Dingzhou to fund a monastic feast for the emperor's longevity.

sentences.zh: 初，北江蠻酋最大者曰彭氏，世有溪州，州有三，曰上、中、下溪，又有龍賜、天賜、忠順、保靜、感化、永順州六，懿、安、遠、新、給、富、來、寧、南、順、高州十一，總二十州，皆置刺史。

translations.literal: At the outset, the greatest chieftain of the Northern River Man was the Peng clan, which for generations held Xi Prefecture; the prefecture had three parts — Upper, Middle, and Lower Xi — and moreover six prefectures: Longci, Tianci, Zhongshun, Baojing, Ganhua, and Yongshun; and eleven prefectures: Yi, An, Yuan, Xin, Gei, Fu, Lai, Ning, Nan, Shun, and Gao — twenty in all, each with a prefect installed.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern River country was dominated by the Pengs, who for generations held Xi territory split into Upper, Middle, and Lower Xi, plus six named domains and eleven more — twenty prefectures in all, each with its own prefect.

sentences.zh: 而以下溪州刺史兼都誓主，十九州皆隸焉，謂之誓下。

translations.literal: The Lower Xi prefect also served as Chief of the Overall Oath, and the nineteen prefectures were all subordinate to him — called "under the oath."
translations.idiomatic: The Lower Xi prefect doubled as covenant chief; the other nineteen prefectures answered to him as "under the oath."

sentences.zh: 州將承襲，都誓主率群酋合議，子孫若弟、侄、親黨之當立者，具州名移辰州為保證，申鈐轄司以聞，乃賜敕告、印符，受命者隔江北望拜謝。

translations.literal: When a prefect was to inherit office, the covenant chief led the group of chiefs in joint deliberation; whichever descendant, younger brother, nephew, or kinsman ought to succeed — listing the prefecture name, they sent a guarantee document to Chenzhou, reported through the Control Office, and only then received imperial patent and seal tallies; the appointee faced north across the river and bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Succession required the covenant chief and allied chiefs to choose the right heir, document the choice through Chenzhou to the control office, and only then receive patent and seals; appointees bowed north across the river in thanks.

sentences.zh: 州有押案副使及校吏，聽自補置。

translations.literal: Each prefecture had a supervising deputy and clerks; they were permitted to fill these posts themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Each domain could appoint its own supervising deputies and clerks.

sentences.zh: 彭氏自允殊、文勇、儒猛相繼為下溪州刺史，至仕漢為殿直，留西京，後輒遁歸。

translations.literal: The Peng clan from Yunshu, Wenyong, and Rumeng in succession served as Lower Xi prefects; when Shihan became Palace Attendant he was kept in the Western Capital, but later abruptly fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Yunshu, Wenyong, and Rumeng had ruled Lower Xi in turn; Shihan, once made palace attendant, was kept at the western capital but soon fled home.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，以狀白辰州，自言父老兄亡，潛歸本道，願放還家屬。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiansheng he reported to Chenzhou, stating himself that his father was aged and his elder brother dead, that he had secretly returned to his circuit, and wished his family released.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiansheng he told Chenzhou his father was old and his brother dead, that he had slipped home, and asked that his family be sent to him.

sentences.zh: 詔徙其家京師，舍以官第。

translations.literal: An edict removed his family to the capital and lodged them in an official residence.
translations.idiomatic: The court moved his family to the capital and housed them in an official residence.

sentences.zh: 未幾，儒猛言仕漢逃歸，誘群蠻為亂，遣別子仕端等殺之。

translations.literal: Before long, Rumeng reported that Shihan had fled back and incited the Man tribes to rebellion; he sent his other son Shiduan and others to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Rumeng reported that Shihan had returned and stirred the tribes to revolt; he sent Shiduan and others to kill him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其忠，降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: The court commended his loyalty and issued an edict of praise and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his loyalty and sent a commending edict.

sentences.zh: 時儒猛為檢校尚書右僕射，特遷左僕射。

translations.literal: At that time Rumeng was Honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; he was specially promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Rumeng, then honorary right vice director, was promoted to the left-hand post.

sentences.zh: 又以仕端為檢校國子祭酒，知溶州，加賜鹽三百斤、彩三十匹。

translations.literal: Shiduan was also made Honorary Director of the Directorate of Education, Administrator of Rong Prefecture, with an additional gift of three hundred jin of salt and thirty bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduan became honorary director of education and prefect of Rong, with three hundred jin of salt and thirty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 彭氏有文綰者，知中彭州，即忠順州也。

translations.literal: Among the Peng clan was Wenwan, who governed Zhong Peng — that is, Zhongshun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Another Peng, Wenwan, ruled Zhong Peng — the same as Zhongshun.

sentences.zh: 三年，儒猛攻殺文綰，其子儒索率其黨九十二人來歸，補儒索復州都知兵馬使，餘官為稟給。

translations.literal: In the third year, Rumeng attacked and killed Wenwan; his son Suo led ninety-two followers to submit; Suo was appointed to restore the prefectural post of overall military commander, and the rest were given stipend offices.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Rumeng killed Wenwan; Suo's ninety-two followers surrendered; Suo was restored as military commander, the rest given stipend posts.

sentences.zh: 五年，儒猛死，仕端以名馬來獻，詔還其馬，命知下溪州，賜以袍帶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Rumeng died; Shiduan presented a famed horse; an edict returned the horse, appointed him to govern Lower Xi, and bestowed robe and belt.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Rumeng died; Shiduan offered a famed horse, which was returned; he was made Lower Xi prefect and given robes and belt.

sentences.zh: 七年，遂以其弟仕羲貢方物。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, his younger brother Shixi then presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven his brother Shixi brought tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 明道初，仕端死，復命仕羲為刺史，累遷檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At the start of Mingdao, Shiduan died; Shixi was again appointed prefect, and was repeatedly promoted to Honorary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiduan died early in Mingdao, Shixi became prefect and rose to honorary right vice director.

sentences.zh: 自允殊至仕羲五世矣。

translations.literal: From Yunshu to Shixi was already five generations.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations had passed from Yunshu to Shixi.

sentences.zh: 仕羲有子師寶，景祐中知忠順州。

translations.literal: Shixi had a son Shibao, who in the Jingyou era governed Zhongshun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shixi's son Shibao governed Zhongshun during Jingyou.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，以罪絕其奉貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli, because of crime his tribute offerings were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli 4 cut off his tribute for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 蓋自咸平以來，始聽二十州納貢，歲有常賜，蠻人以為利，有罪則絕之。

translations.literal: Generally from Xianping onward the twenty prefectures were first permitted to present tribute with annual regular gifts; the Man regarded this as profit, and when guilty tribute was terminated.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xianping the twenty domains had paid tribute for fixed yearly gifts — a profit the Man prized, withdrawn when they offended.

sentences.zh: 其後，師寶數自訴，請知上溪州。

translations.literal: Thereafter Shibao repeatedly pleaded on his own behalf, requesting to govern Upper Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shibao repeatedly petitioned to rule Upper Xi.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，始從其請，朝貢如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou his request was first granted; court tribute resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyou 2 granted his wish and restored his tribute rights.

sentences.zh: 既而師寶妻為仕羲取去，師寶忿恚。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Shibao's wife was taken by Shixi; Shibao was resentful and enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shixi took Shibao's wife; Shibao was furious.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，與其子知龍賜州師黨舉族趨辰州，告其父之惡；

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe, he and his son Shidang, who governed Longci Prefecture, led their entire clan to Chenzhou to report his father's wicked deeds;
translations.idiomatic: Zhihe 2 he and his son Shidang of Longci led the whole clan to Chenzhou to denounce his father;

sentences.zh: 且言仕羲嘗殺誓下十三州將，奪其符印，並有其地，貢奉賜予悉專之，自號如意大王，補置官屬，將起為亂。

translations.literal: and stated that Shixi had once killed the commanders of thirteen oath-subordinate prefectures, seized their tallies and seals, and taken their lands as well, monopolizing tribute and gifts, styling himself the Great King of As-You-Will, appointing officials, and about to rise in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: charging that Shixi had killed thirteen subordinate chiefs, seized their seals and lands, hoarded tribute and gifts, styled himself Great King As-You-Will, appointed officials, and planned rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於是知辰州宋守信與通判賈師熊、轉運使李肅之合議，率兵數千，深入討伐，以師寶為鄉導。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song Shouxin, Administrator of Chen, Vice-Prefect Jia Shixiong, and Transport Commissioner Li Suzhi jointly deliberated, led several thousand troops on a deep punitive expedition, and used Shibao as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Chen prefect Song Shouxin, vice-prefect Jia Shixiong, and transport commissioner Li Suzhi led several thousand men deep into the hills with Shibao as guide.

sentences.zh: 兵至而仕羲遁入他峒，不可得，俘其孥及銅柱，而官軍戰死者十六七，守信等皆坐貶。

translations.literal: When the army arrived Shixi slipped into another ravine and could not be taken; his family and the bronze pillar were captured, but six or seven tenths of the government troops died in battle; Shouxin and others were all punished by demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Shixi escaped to another gorge; the army seized his family and the bronze pillar but lost six or seven men in ten; Shouxin and his colleagues were demoted.

sentences.zh: 自是，蠻獠數入寇鈔，邊吏不能制。

translations.literal: From this time the Man and Liao repeatedly entered to raid and plunder; frontier officials could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Man and Liao raiders harried the borders beyond local control.

sentences.zh: 朝廷姑欲無事，間遣吏諭旨，許以改過自歸，裁損五七州貢奉歲賜。

translations.literal: The court for the time being wished for no trouble; from time to time it sent officials to convey the imperial will, permitting them to reform and return of themselves, and trimmed the annual gifts of five or seven prefectures' tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Preferring peace, the court occasionally sent envoys offering amnesty and trimmed gifts to five or seven domains.

sentences.zh: 初輒不聽，後遣三司副使李參、文思副使竇舜卿、侍御史朱處約、轉運使王綽經制，大出兵臨之，且馳檄招諭。

translations.literal: At first they repeatedly would not listen; later the Vice Commissioner of the Three Departments Li Can, Vice Commissioner of the Literary Exchanges Dou Shunqing, Attending Censor Zhu Chuyue, and Transport Commissioner Wang Chuo were sent to oversee; a large army was brought to bear, and at the same time proclamations were hurried out to summon and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: They refused at first; later Li Can, Dou Shunqing, Zhu Chuyue, and Wang Chuo took command with a large force and simultaneous summons.

sentences.zh: 而仕羲乃陳本無反狀，其僭稱號、補官屬，特遠人不知中國禮義而然。

translations.literal: Shixi then stated that he had had no rebellious intent; his assuming titles and appointing officials was merely because distant people did not know Central Court ritual and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Shixi protested he had never rebelled — titles and appointments were mere ignorance of court ritual.

sentences.zh: 守信等輕信師寶之譖，擅伐無辜，願以二十州舊地復貢奉內屬。

translations.literal: Shouxin and others lightly believed Shibao's slander and made war on the innocent without authority; he wished to restore the old lands of the twenty prefectures to tribute and inner submission.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed Shouxin for trusting Shibao's lies and attacking the innocent, and offered to restore all twenty domains to tribute and allegiance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又遣殿中丞雷簡夫往視之。

translations.literal: The court again dispatched Palace Ceremonialist-in-Ordinary Lei Jianfu to inspect on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent palace official Lei Jianfu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，仕羲乃歸所掠兵丁五十一人、械甲千八百九事，率蠻眾七百飲血就降，辰州亦還其孥及銅柱。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, Shixi then returned fifty-one soldier captives he had seized and 1,809 pieces of armor and weapons, led seven hundred Man to drink blood and submit, and Chenzhou also returned his family and the bronze pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 2 he returned fifty-one soldiers and 1,809 arms, led seven hundred tribesmen in a blood oath to surrender; Chenzhou restored his family and the bronze pillar.

sentences.zh: 時師寶已死，遣師黨歸知龍賜州，戒勿殺。

translations.literal: At that time Shibao was already dead; Shidang was sent back to govern Longci Prefecture with an injunction not to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Shibao was already dead; Shidang was sent home to rule Longci with orders not to kill.

sentences.zh: 自是，仕羲歲奉職貢。

translations.literal: From this time Shixi annually presented official tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Shixi paid yearly tribute.

sentences.zh: 然黠驁，數盜邊，即辰州界白馬崖下喏溪聚眾據守，朝廷數招諭，令歸侵地，不聽。

translations.literal: Yet he was cunning and fierce, repeatedly raiding the border; just within Chenzhou's boundary below Baima Cliff at Nuoxi he gathered crowds and held position; the court repeatedly summoned and instructed him to return encroached lands, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning and unruly, he raided repeatedly from Nuoxi below Baima Cliff inside Chen's border; repeated summons to return seized land went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，為其子師彩所弑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining he was murdered by his son Shicai.
translations.idiomatic: Xining 3 his son Shicai killed him.

sentences.zh: 師彩專為暴虐，其兄師晏攻殺之，並誅其黨，納誓表於朝，並上仕羲平生鞍馬、器服，仍歸喏溪地，乃命師晏襲州事。

translations.literal: Shicai devoted himself to cruelty and violence; his elder brother Shiyan attacked and killed him, also executed his faction, submitted the oath memorial to court, and presented Shixi's lifetime saddles, horses, and attire, also returning Nuoxi lands; Shiyan was then ordered to inherit prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shicai ruled by terror until his brother Shiyan killed him and his faction, submitted the oath memorial, returned Shixi's goods and Nuoxi land, and took over the domain.

sentences.zh: 五年，復以馬皮、白峒地來獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again presented horse hides and Baidong territory.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he offered horse hides and Baidong land.

sentences.zh: 詔進為下溪州刺史，賜母妻封邑。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to Lower Xi Prefect and bestowed enfeoffments on his mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Lower Xi prefect; his mother and wife received fiefs.

sentences.zh: 章惇經制南、北江，湖北提點刑獄李平招納師晏，誓下州峒蠻張景謂、彭德儒、向永勝、覃文猛、覃彥霸各以其地歸版籍，師晏遂降。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun administered the Southern and Northern Rivers; Hubei Judicial Intendant Li Ping recruited Shiyan; Man of oath-subordinate prefectures Zhang Jingxu, Peng Deru, Xiang Yongsheng, Tan Wenmeng, and Tan Yanba each returned their lands to the registers, and Shiyan then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun oversaw both rivers; Li Ping won over Shiyan while Zhang Jingxu, Peng Deru, Xiang Yongsheng, Tan Wenmeng, and Tan Yanba surrendered their lands — and Shiyan yielded.

sentences.zh: 詔修築下溪州城，並置砦於茶灘南岸，賜新城名會溪，新砦名黔安，戍以兵，隸辰州，出租賦如漢民。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the construction of Lower Xi city and also the establishment of a fort on the south bank of Chatan; the new city was named Huixi, the new fort Qian'an; garrisoned with troops, subordinate to Chenzhou, levying rent and tax like Han subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Lower Xi city and a fort on Chatan's south bank were built — Huixi and Qian'an — garrisoned, subject to Chen, taxed like Han settlers.

sentences.zh: 遣師晏詣闕，授禮賓副使、京東州都監，官其下六十有四人。

translations.literal: Shiyan was sent to the capital, appointed Vice Commissioner of Ritual Guests and Overall Supervisor of Jingdong Prefectures; sixty-four men under him were given offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan went to court as vice commissioner of ritual guests and Jingdong supervisor; sixty-four followers received posts.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，湖北轉運司言辰州江外生蠻覃仕穩等願內附，詔不許招納。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, the Hubei Transport Office reported that the raw Man beyond the river at Chenzhou, Tan Shiwen and others, wished to submit inward; an edict did not permit recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng 8 Hubei transport reported Chen raw Man including Tan Shiwen seeking allegiance; the court forbade recruiting them.

sentences.zh: 其後彭仕誠者復為都誓主。

translations.literal: Thereafter Peng Shicheng again became Chief of the Overall Oath.
translations.idiomatic: Later Peng Shicheng again became covenant chief.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，羅家蠻寇鈔，詔召仕誠及都頭覃文懿等至辰州約敕之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou, the Luojia Man raided and plundered; an edict summoned Shicheng and Regiment Chief Tan Wenyi and others to Chenzhou for binding instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 3 Luojia raiders struck; Shicheng, Tan Wenyi, and other chiefs were summoned to Chenzhou and bound by edict.

sentences.zh: 四年，知誓下保靜州彭儒武、知永順州彭儒同、知謂州彭思聰、知龍賜州彭允宗、知藍州彭土明、知吉州彭儒崇，各同其州押案副使進奉興龍節及冬至、正旦溪布有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Peng Ruwu, Administrator of oath-subordinate Baojing; Peng Rutong of Yongshun; Peng Sicong of Wei; Peng Yunzong of Longci; Peng Tuming of Lan; and Peng Ruchong of Ji — each together with his prefecture's supervising deputy presented tribute for the Ascension festival, winter solstice, and new year's day with graded stream-cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Year four six Peng prefects and their deputies sent graded stream-cloth for the Ascension festival, solstice, and New Year.

sentences.zh: 初，熙寧中，天子方用兵以威四夷，湖北提點刑獄趙鼎言峽州峒首刻剝亡度，蠻眾願內屬。

translations.literal: At the outset, in the Xining era, the Son of Heaven was just then using arms to awe the four Yi; Hubei Judicial Intendant Zhao Ding stated that the ravine chief of Xia Prefecture extorted without limit and the Man masses wished to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining the emperor was bullying the frontier tribes; Zhao Ding reported that a Xia gorge chief had extorted his people past endurance and they wished to submit.

sentences.zh: 辰州布衣張翹亦上書言南、北江利害，遂以章惇察訪湖北，經制蠻事。

translations.literal: A Chenzhou commoner Zhang Qiao also memorialized on the gains and harms of the Southern and Northern Rivers; Zhang Dun was therefore sent to inspect Hubei and administer Man affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen commoner Zhang Qiao wrote on both rivers; Zhang Dun was sent to inspect Hubei and take charge of Man affairs.

sentences.zh: 而南江之舒氏、北江之彭氏、梅山之蘇氏、誠州之楊氏相繼納土，創立城砦，使之比內地為王民。

translations.literal: The Shu clan of the Southern River, the Peng clan of the Northern River, the Su clan of Meishan, and the Yang clan of Cheng Prefecture in succession offered their lands; fortified cities and forts were established so they might be like the interior in becoming the king's people.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu of the south, Peng of the north, Su of Meishan, and Yang of Cheng surrendered in turn; new forts and garrisons made them subjects like any interior county.

sentences.zh: 北江彭氏已見前。

translations.literal: The Northern River Peng clan has already been seen above.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern River Pengs have already been discussed above.

sentences.zh: 南江諸蠻自辰州達於長沙、邵陽，各有溪峒：曰敘、曰峽、曰中勝、曰元，則舒氏居之；

translations.literal: The various Southern River Man from Chenzhou reaching to Changsha and Shaoyang each had stream-caves: called Xu, Xia, Zhongsheng, and Yuan — the Shu clan dwelt in these;
translations.idiomatic: Southern River Man from Chen to Changsha and Shaoyang held domains named Xu, Xia, Zhongsheng, and Yuan — all Shu country;

sentences.zh: 曰獎、曰錦、曰懿、曰晃，則田氏居之；

translations.literal: called Jiang, Jin, Yi, and Huang — the Tian clan dwelt in these;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, Jin, Yi, and Huang belonged to the Tians;

sentences.zh: 曰富、曰鶴、曰保順、曰天賜、曰古，則向氏居之。

translations.literal: called Fu, He, Baoshun, Tianci, and Gu — the Xiang clan dwelt in these.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, He, Baoshun, Tianci, and Gu were Xiang lands.

sentences.zh: 舒氏則德郛、德言、君疆、光銀，田氏則處達、漢瓊、漢希、漢能、漢權、保金，向氏則通漢、光普、行猛、永豐、永晤，皆受朝命。

translations.literal: Among the Shu were Defu, Deyan, Junjiang, and Guangyin; among the Tian were Chuda, Hanqiong, Hanxi, Hanneng, Hanquan, and Baojin; among the Xiang were Tonghan, Guangpu, Xingmeng, Yongfeng, and Yongwu — all received court appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Defu, Deyan, Junjiang, and Guangyin led the Shu; Chuda, Hanqiong, Hanxi, Hanneng, Hanquan, and Baojin the Tians; Tonghan, Guangpu, Xingmeng, Yongfeng, and Yongwu the Xiangs — all held court rank.

sentences.zh: 自治平末，光銀入貢。

translations.literal: From the end of Zhiping, Guangyin presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyin had been sending tribute since late Zhiping.

sentences.zh: 故事，南江諸蠻亦隸辰州，貢進則給以驛券，光銀援以為請，詔以券九道給之。

translations.literal: By precedent the Southern River Man also were subordinate to Chenzhou; when tribute was presented courier vouchers were issued; Guangyin cited this in a request; an edict granted nine vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: Southern River tribute had always earned courier vouchers from Chen; Guangyin cited precedent and received nine vouchers.

sentences.zh: 其後有峽州舒光秀者，以刻剝其眾不附。

translations.literal: Thereafter there was Shuguangxiu of Xia Prefecture among the Shu, who because of exploiting his people excessively was not obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shu chief Shuguangxiu of Xia lost his people by extortion.

sentences.zh: 張翹言：「南江諸蠻雖有十六州之地，惟富、峽、敘僅有千戶，餘不滿百，土廣無兵，加以薦饑。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiao stated: "Although the Southern River Man have territory of sixteen prefectures, only Fu, Xia, and Xu have as many as a thousand households; the rest do not reach a hundred; the land is broad but without soldiers, and in addition there is repeated famine from pestilence."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiao wrote: "Sixteen Southern River domains exist, but only Fu, Xia, and Xu have a thousand households; the rest count fewer than a hundred; the land is wide, arms few, and pestilence has brought famine."

sentences.zh: 近向永晤與繡、鶴、敘諸州蠻自相仇殺，眾苦之，咸思歸化。

translations.literal: Recently Yongwu of the Xiang clan and the Man of Xiu, He, Xu, and other prefectures have mutually feuded and killed one another; the masses suffer from this and all wish to submit and be transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Yongwu and the Xiu, He, and Xu tribes have feuded until the people crave submission.

sentences.zh: 願先招富、峽二州，俾納土，則餘州自歸，並及彭師晏之孱弱，皆可郡縣。

translations.literal: He wished first to recruit Fu and Xia, the two prefectures, to offer their lands; then the remaining prefectures would return of themselves, and even the weakness of Peng Shiyan could all be made into prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: "Win Fu and Xia first, and the rest will follow — even weak Peng Shiyan's domains could become regular counties."

sentences.zh: 」詔下知辰州劉策商度，策請如翹言。

translations.literal: " An edict was sent down to Liu Ce, Administrator of Chenzhou, for deliberation; Ce requested to act as Qiao had said.
translations.idiomatic: The order went to Liu Ce at Chen; Ce endorsed Zhang's plan.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，乃遣章惇察訪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, Zhang Dun was then dispatched on an inspection tour.
translations.idiomatic: Xining 5 brought Zhang Dun's inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 未幾，策卒，乃以東作坊使石鑒為湖北鈐轄兼知辰州，且助惇經制。

translations.literal: Before long Ce died; the Eastern Workshops Commissioner Shi Jian was then made Hubei Control Commissioner while also Administrator of Chenzhou, and assisted Dun in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ce soon died; workshop commissioner Shi Jian became Hubei control commissioner and Chen prefect to aid Zhang.

sentences.zh: 明年，富州向永晤獻先朝所賜劍及印來歸順，繼而光銀、光秀等亦降。

translations.literal: The next year Xiang Yongwu of Fu presented the sword and seal bestowed by the former court and came to submit; thereafter Guangyin, Guangxiu, and others also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Yongwu of Fu surrendered his patent sword and seal; Guangyin and Guangxiu followed.

sentences.zh: 獨田氏有元猛者，頗桀驁難製，異時數侵奪舒、向二族地。

translations.literal: Only the Tian clan had Yuanmeng, who was quite fierce and hard to control; at other times he repeatedly encroached on and seized lands of the Shu and Xiang clans.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tian Yuanmeng remained proud and ungovernable, long encroaching on Shu and Xiang lands.

sentences.zh: 惇遣左侍禁李資將輕兵往招諭。

translations.literal: Dun dispatched Left Palace Guard Li Zi to lead light troops to go summon and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent guard Li Zi with a light detachment to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 資，辰州流人，曩與張翹同獻策者也。

translations.literal: Zi was a Chenzhou exile who in the past had joined Zhang Qiao in presenting the same strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was a Chen exile who had once advised Zhang Qiao.

sentences.zh: 褊宕無謀，褻慢夷獠，遂為懿、洽州蠻所殺。

translations.literal: Narrow-minded and rash without strategy, disrespectful toward the Yi and Liao, he was thereupon killed by the Man of Yi and Qia prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Petty, rash, and contemptuous of the tribes, he was killed by Yi and Qia Man.

sentences.zh: 惇進兵破懿州，南江州峒悉平，遂置沅州，以懿州新城為治所，尋又置誠州。

translations.literal: Dun advanced troops and smashed Yi Prefecture; the Southern River prefectures and ravines were all pacified; Yuan Prefecture was then established with Yi Prefecture's new city as seat, and shortly thereafter Cheng Prefecture was also established.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang stormed Yi; the Southern River was pacified; Yuan Prefecture was created at Yi's new city, then Cheng as well.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，傅堯俞、王岩叟言：「沅、誠州創建以來，設官屯兵，布列砦縣，募役人，調戍兵，費钜萬，公私騷然，荊湖兩路為之空竭。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou, Fu Yaoyu and Wang Yansou stated: "Since the founding of Yuan and Cheng prefectures, officials have been established, troops garrisoned, forts and counties laid out, corvée laborers recruited, frontier guards transferred — expenses in the tens of thousands; public and private are in turmoil; the two circuits of Jing and Hu are emptied for it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou Fu Yaoyu and Wang Yansou wrote: "Yuan and Cheng have cost tens of thousands — officials, garrisons, forts, corvée, rotating troops — draining Jing and Hu."

sentences.zh: 又自廣西融州創開道路達誠州，增置潯江等堡，其地無所有，湖、廣移賦以給一方，民不安業，願斟酌廢置。

translations.literal: Moreover, from Guangxi Rong Prefecture a road was newly opened reaching Cheng Prefecture, and forts such as Xunjiang were added; the land has nothing to offer; Hunan and Guang move tax levies to supply one corner; the people have no secure livelihood — they wish careful consideration of abolition."
translations.idiomatic: "A road from Guangxi's Rong to Cheng and new forts like Xunjiang bring nothing in return while Hunan and Guangxi ship taxes to sustain the region — the people beg for reconsideration."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以沅州建置至是十五年，蠻情安習已久，但廢誠州為渠陽軍，而沅州至今為郡。

translations.literal: " The court held that Yuan Prefecture's establishment had by then been fifteen years and Man sentiment had long been settled and accustomed; only Cheng Prefecture was abolished as Quyang Commandery, while Yuan Prefecture to this day remains a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years the Man were settled; Cheng became Quyang commandery, but Yuan remains a prefecture today.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，諸蠻復叛，朝廷方務休息，痛懲邀功生事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou the various Man rebelled again; the court was then pursuing repose and sternly punished those who sought merit by stirring up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou the Man rose again, but the court wanted peace and cracked down hard on officers who manufactured incidents to win credit.

sentences.zh: 廣西張整、融州溫嵩坐擅殺蠻人，皆置之罪。

translations.literal: Zhang Zheng of Guangxi and Wen Song of Rong Prefecture were convicted of killing Man without authorization; both were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng in Guangxi and Wen Song of Rong were punished for killing Man on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 詔諭湖南、北及廣西路曰：「國家疆理四海，務在柔遠。

translations.literal: An edict instructed Hunan, North Hunan, and the Guangxi circuit, saying: "The state maps and governs the four seas; its task lies in treating distant peoples gently.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to Hunan, northern Hunan, and Guangxi: "The empire holds all within the seas; its duty is to win over those far away."

sentences.zh: 頃湖、廣諸蠻近漢者無所統壹，因其請吏，量置城邑以撫治之。

translations.literal: Recently the Man of Hunan and Guang near the Han had no single governance; because they requested officials, towns were proportionally established to pacify and govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the Man of Hunan and Guang who lived close to Han settlements had lacked unified rule; at their request for officials, the court had set up towns as needed to govern them.

sentences.zh: 邊臣邀功獻議，創通融州道路，侵逼峒穴，致生疑懼。

translations.literal: Frontier officers seeking merit offered plans, opened a road through Rong Prefecture, pressed upon cave settlements, and bred suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officers hungry for credit proposed opening a road through Rong, pressing on cave settlements until fear and distrust spread.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其無用，旋即廢罷；

translations.literal: The court knew this useless and at once abolished it;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no benefit, the court abolished the project at once;

sentences.zh: 邊吏失於撫遏，遂爾扇搖。

translations.literal: border officials failed in pacification and restraint, and so stirred up unrest.
translations.idiomatic: but border officials had failed to pacify and restrain them, and unrest spread in turn.

sentences.zh: 其叛酋楊晟台等並免追討，諸路所開道路、創置堡砦並廢。

translations.literal: The rebel chiefs Yang ShengTai and others were all exempted from pursuit; roads opened and forts newly built on every route were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chiefs such as Yang ShengTai were spared pursuit, and every new road and fort along the circuits was dismantled.

sentences.zh: 」自後，五溪郡縣棄而不問。

translations.literal: " Thereafter the commanderies and counties of Wuxi were abandoned and left unaddressed.
translations.idiomatic: " After that the commanderies and counties of the Five Streams were left to themselves.

sentences.zh: 崇寧以來，開邊拓土之議復熾，於是安化上三州及思廣洞蒙光明、樂安峒程大法、都丹團黃光明、靖州西道楊再立、辰州覃都管罵等各願納土輸貢賦。

translations.literal: Since Chongning the talk of opening borders and expanding territory flared again; then Anhua's upper three prefectures; Meng Guangming of Siguang cave; Cheng Dafa of Le'an ravine; Huang Guangming of the Dudan regiment; Yang Zaili of Jingzhou's western route; Tan Du, Chenzhou overseer; and others each wished to submit their land and pay tribute and taxes.
