translations.idiomatic: From Chongning onward the push to open borders and seize land revived; Anhua's upper three prefectures, Meng Guangming of Siguang cave, Cheng Dafa of Le'an ravine, Huang Guangming of the Dudan regiment, Yang Zaili on Jingzhou's western route, Tan Du of Chenzhou, and others all offered to surrender their lands and pay taxes.

sentences.zh: 又令廣西招納左、右江四百五十餘峒。

translations.literal: Guangxi was also ordered to recruit and absorb more than four hundred fifty ravines of the Left and Right Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi was told to bring in more than four hundred fifty ravines along the Left and Right Rivers.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，議者以為「招致熟蕃，接武請吏，竭金帛、繒絮以啖其欲，捐高爵、厚奉以侈其心。

translations.literal: In Xuanhe, memorialists said: "Summoning seasoned Fan, one after another they request officials; gold, silk, and floss are exhausted to feed their desires, high ranks and rich stipends are lavished to inflate their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe critics argued: "We lure in acculturated Fan who then line up to demand officials, drain gold, silk, and floss to satisfy their appetites, and heap rank and salary on them until their ambitions swell."

sentences.zh: 開闢荒蕪，草創城邑，張皇事勢，僥幸賞恩。

translations.literal: Wasteland is opened, cities are founded from nothing, affairs are trumped up grandly, and rewards and favor are hoped for by chance.
translations.idiomatic: They clear wilderness, throw up new towns, inflate every undertaking, and gamble on imperial reward.

sentences.zh: 入版圖者存虛名，充府庫者亡實利。

translations.literal: Those entering the registers keep empty names; what fills the treasuries yields no real profit.
translations.idiomatic: What enters the registers is a hollow name; what fills the treasuries brings no real gain.

sentences.zh: 不毛之地，既不可耕；

translations.literal: Barren ground cannot be farmed;
translations.idiomatic: The soil will not bear crops;

sentences.zh: 狼子野心，頑冥莫革。

translations.literal: wolf-cub hearts remain; stubborn and dark, they will not change.
translations.idiomatic: their hearts are those of wolf cubs—stubborn and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 建築之後，西南夷獠交寇，而溪峒子蠻亦復跳梁。

translations.literal: After the construction, southwestern Yi and Liao raided in turn, and the stream-cave Man also rose in revolt again.
translations.idiomatic: Once the building began, Yi and Liao in the southwest raided back and forth, and the stream-cave Man rose in revolt again.

sentences.zh: 士卒死於干戈，官吏沒於王事，肝腦塗地，往往有之。

translations.literal: Soldiers died by arms, officials perished in the king's service; brains and guts smeared the ground—this was often seen.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers fell to weapons, officials died on the throne's business, and brains and guts stained the earth—again and again.

sentences.zh: 以此知納土之義，非徒無益，而又害之所由生也。

translations.literal: From this one knows that submitting land is not merely without benefit but also the source from which harm arises.
translations.idiomatic: This showed that accepting surrendered territory was not merely useless but the very seed of harm.

sentences.zh: 莫若俾帥臣、監司條具建築以來財用出入之數，商較利病，可省者省，可並者並，減戍兵漕運，而夷狄可撫，邊鄙可亡患矣！

translations.literal: Better to have circuit commanders and supervisory officials itemize revenues and expenditures since construction, weigh benefits and harms, reduce what can be reduced and merge what can be merged, cut garrison troops and grain transport—then Yi and Di may be pacified and border troubles may vanish!
translations.idiomatic: Better let commanders and supervisors list every cost since construction, weigh gain against loss, cut and combine where possible, trim garrisons and transport—then the tribes could be soothed and the frontier freed of trouble!"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔悉廢所置初郡。

translations.literal: " An edict then abolished all the new prefectures that had been established.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then abolished every newly created prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其餘諸蠻，自乾興以來，或叛或服，其類不一，各以歲月次之。

translations.literal: The remaining Man from Qianxing on, sometimes rebelled and sometimes submitted, not all of one kind; each is set out below by year.
translations.idiomatic: Other Man affairs from Qianxing onward—now rebellion, now submission, no single pattern—are recorded below in chronological order.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，順州蠻田彥晏率其黨田承恩寇施州暗利砦，縱火而去，夔州發兵擊之，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Early Qianxing, Tian Yanyan of Shunzhou Man led his follower Tian Chengen to raid Anli stockade in Shizhou, set fires and left; Kuizhou sent troops to strike them and took many captives.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianxing, Shunzhou Man Tian Yanyan and his man Tian Chengen raided Shizhou's Anli stockade, torched it, and fled; Kuizhou troops struck back and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 彥晏在真宗朝為歸德將軍、檢校太子賓客、知順州；

translations.literal: Yanyan in Emperor Zhenzong's reign had been General of Guiding Virtue, Honorary Guest of the Heir Apparent, and Administrator of Shunzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yanyan had served Zhenzong as General of Guiding Virtue, honorary heir-apparent guest, and prefect of Shun;

sentences.zh: 承恩者，知保順州田彥曉子也。

translations.literal: Chengen was the son of Tian Yanxiao, Administrator of Baoshun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen was the son of Baoshun prefect Tian Yanxiao.

sentences.zh: 明年，彥晏款邊上誓狀，願還所掠金帛、器械，且輸粟二千石自贖。

translations.literal: The next year Yanyan came to the border with a sworn petition, wishing to return looted gold, silk, and weapons, and moreover to offer two thousand piculs of grain to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yanyan came to the border with a sworn petition, offering to return plundered gold, silk, and arms and pay two thousand piculs of grain as ransom.

sentences.zh: 詔拒其粟，舍其所負金帛，第令歸掠去戶口。

translations.literal: An edict refused the grain, remitted the gold and silk he owed, and only ordered the return of abducted population.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused the grain, forgave the gold and silk, and required only the return of captives.

sentences.zh: 仍加彥晏寧遠將軍、檢校工部尚書，承恩檢校國子祭酒兼監察御史，皆知州如故。

translations.literal: Yanyan was further made General of Pacifying the Far, Honorary Minister of Works; Chengen Honorary Libationer of the Imperial Academy with concurrent Investigating Censor; both remained Administrators as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyan was promoted to General of Pacifying the Far and honorary minister of works; Chengen to honorary imperial-academy libationer and investigating censor—both kept their prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後又有田忠顯者，與其黨百九人入貢。

translations.literal: Later there was also Tian Zhongxian, who with his party of one hundred nine persons came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tian Zhongxian arrived with a party of one hundred nine to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年，知古州向光普自言，嘗創佛寺，請名報國，歲度僧一人，許之。

translations.literal: Tiansheng year 2, Xiang Guangpu, Administrator of Gu Prefecture, stated he had once founded a Buddhist temple and asked the name Baoguo (Repaying the State), with one monk ordained yearly—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiansheng, Gu prefect Xiang Guangpu reported that he had built a temple and asked that it be named Repaying the State, with one ordination each year—granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，歸順等州蠻田思欽等以方物來獻，時來者三百一人，而夔州路轉運司不先以聞，詔劾之。

translations.literal: Year 4, Tian Siqin and other Man of Guishun and other prefectures brought local products as tribute; those who came then numbered three hundred one, but the Kuizhou circuit transport office did not report in advance—an edict ordered impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Tian Siqin and other Man of Guishun brought tribute; three hundred one came, yet the Kuizhou transport office failed to report beforehand—the court ordered an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 既而又詔安、遠、天賜、保順、南、順等州蠻貢京師，道里遼遠而離寒暑之苦，其聽以貢物留施州，所賜就給之。

translations.literal: Then again an edict: when Man of An, Yuan, Tianci, Baoshun, Nan, Shun, and other prefectures tribute to the capital—the road being long and far from the trials of cold and heat—let them leave tribute goods at Shizhou and receive gifts there.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict allowed Man of An, Yuan, Tianci, Baoshun, Nan, Shun, and the like, rather than travel the long road to the capital through heat and cold, to leave tribute at Shizhou and take their gifts there.

sentences.zh: 願入貢者十人，聽三二人至闕下，首領聽三年一至。

translations.literal: Of ten wishing to tribute, two or three might come to court; chiefs were permitted once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Of every ten who wished to come, only two or three might reach court; chiefs might come once every three years.

sentences.zh: 七年，黔州蠻、舒延蠻、繡州蠻向光緒皆來貢。

translations.literal: Year 7, Qianzhou Man, Shuyan Man, and Xiuzhou Man Xiang Guangxu all came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Qian Man, Shuyan Man, and Xiuzhou's Xiang Guangxu all presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 九年，施州屬蠻覃彥綰等寇永寧砦。

translations.literal: Year 9, dependent Man of Shizhou Tan Yanwan and others raided Yongning stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year dependent Shizhou Man led by Tan Yanwan attacked Yongning stockade.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，澧州屬蠻五百餘人入寇。

translations.literal: In Jingyou, more than five hundred dependent Man of Lizhou raided inward.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingyou more than five hundred dependent Lizhou Man raided inward.

sentences.zh: 時州將崔承祐畏避不以聞，為荊湖鈐轄司所奏，詔劾罷之。

translations.literal: The prefectural commander Cui Chengyou shrank away and did not report; memorialized by the Jing-Hu Control Commission—an edict ordered impeachment and removal.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural commander Cui Chengyou shrank from reporting it; the Jing-Hu control commission memorialized against him, and he was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 寶元二年，辰州狤獠三千餘人款附，以州將張昭懿招輯有功，進一官。

translations.literal: Baoyuan year 2, more than three thousand Jieliao of Chenzhou submitted; the prefectural commander Zhang Zhaoyi was promoted one rank for successful recruitment and gathering.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoyuan more than three thousand Jieliao of Chen submitted; prefect Zhang Zhaoyi was promoted one rank for winning them in.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，桂陽監蠻徭內寇，詔發兵捕擊之。

translations.literal: Qingli year 3, Guiyang Directorate Man-Yao raided inward—an edict ordered troops sent to capture and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingli Guiyang Man-Yao raided inward, and the court sent troops to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 蠻徭者，居山谷間，其山自衡州常寧縣屬於桂陽、郴連賀韶四州，環紆千餘里，蠻居其中，不事賦役，謂之徭人。

translations.literal: The Man-Yao dwell in mountain valleys; their mountains from Changning County, Hengzhou, extend through Guiyang and the four prefectures Chen, Lian, He, and Shao—winding over a thousand li with Man dwelling within, not paying tax and corvée, called Yao people.
translations.idiomatic: The Man-Yao lived in the valleys; from Hengzhou's Changning their mountains ran through Guiyang and Chen, Lian, He, and Shao—a thousand li of winding country where Man paid no taxes and were called Yao.

sentences.zh: 初，有吉州巫黃捉鬼與其兄弟數人皆習蠻法，往來常寧，出入溪峒，誘蠻眾數百人盜販鹽，殺官軍，逃匿峒中，既招出而殺之，又徙山下民他處。

translations.literal: At first there was Jizhou shaman Huang Zhuogui; he and several brothers all practiced Man methods, traveled Changning, entered and left stream-caves, induced several hundred Man to smuggle salt, killed government troops, and fled into caves; after they were lured out and killed, people at the mountain foot were moved elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Jizhou shaman, Huang Zhuogui, and his brothers had learned Man ways, moved through Changning's ravines, and led hundreds of Man to smuggle salt and kill troops; when they were lured out and executed, lowland settlers were relocated.

sentences.zh: 至是，其黨遂合五千人，出桂陽藍山縣華陰峒，害巡檢李延祚、潭州都監張克明。

translations.literal: At this their faction mustered five thousand, emerged from Huayin ravine in Lanshan County, Guiyang, and killed patrol commissioner Li Yanzu and Tanzhou capital director Zhang Keming.
translations.idiomatic: Now their faction mustered five thousand, burst from Huayin ravine in Guiyang's Lanshan, and killed patrol commissioner Li Yanzu and Tanzhou director Zhang Keming.

sentences.zh: 事聞，擢楊畋提點刑獄，督攻討事，久之不克。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Yang Tian was elevated to Judicial Intendant to supervise attack and pacification; for long he could not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Yang Tian was made judicial intendant to lead the campaign, but for a long time could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 遂詔湖南轉運使郭輔之等招撫之，始於湖南置安撫司。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Hunan transport commissioner Guo Fuzhi and others to recruit and pacify them; the Hunan Pacification Commission was first established.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Hunan transport commissioner Guo Fuzhi and others to win them over by persuasion, and for the first time set up a Hunan pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 蠻所至殺掠居民，縱火劫財物，被害者甚眾。

translations.literal: Wherever the Man went they killed and plundered residents, set fires and seized goods—victims were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the Man went they killed, looted, and burned; casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 詔被害者並入山捕蠻，土兵蠲復有差。

translations.literal: An edict allowed all victims to enter the mountains to catch Man; native soldiers received graded exemptions.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were permitted to join the hunt in the hills; native levies received graded tax relief.

sentences.zh: 初，發兵捕蠻，至或誤殺良民，仁宗命訪之，口給絹五匹，仍拊其家。

translations.literal: At first when troops were sent to catch Man they sometimes killed good people by mistake; Renzong ordered inquiry, five bolts of silk per person, and comfort for their families.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the campaign troops sometimes killed innocents; Renzong ordered an inquiry, five bolts of silk for each life lost, and relief for the families.

sentences.zh: 時蠻勢方熾，又遣殿中侍御史王絲、三司度支副使徐的經制。

translations.literal: Man power was then blazing; Palace Diarist Wang Si and Fiscal Vice Commissioner Xu Di were also dispatched to take overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: With Man strength at its height, the court also sent palace diarist Wang Si and fiscal vice commissioner Xu Di to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 降敕書委知潭州劉沆招諭，能自歸者第錄以官。

translations.literal: An imperial letter was sent commissioning Tanzhou Administrator Liu Kang to summon and instruct; those who could return of themselves would be registered and given office.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter charged Tanzhou prefect Liu Kang to offer terms: whoever surrendered would be registered and given rank.

sentences.zh: 沆大發兵臨之，以敕書從事，降二千餘人，使散居所部，錄其首領鄧文誌、黃文晟、黃士元皆為三班奉職。

translations.literal: Kang greatly deployed troops against them, acted by the letter, and more than two thousand surrendered; he had them disperse to their districts and registered leaders Deng Wenzhi, Huang Wensheng, and Huang Shiyuan all as Third-Class Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Kang marched in force under the letter's authority; more than two thousand surrendered and were sent home, while leaders Deng Wenzhi, Huang Wensheng, and Huang Shiyuan were made third-class attendants.

sentences.zh: 又以內殿承製亓贇、崇班胡元嘗在石硋峒捕殺有勞，進贇莊宅副使，元禮賓副使，時四年冬也。

translations.literal: Inner Hall Commissioner Qi Yun and Court Gentleman Hu Yuan had merit capturing and killing at Shi'e ravine—Yun was promoted Vice Commissioner of Manor Houses and Yuan Vice Commissioner of Rites; this was in the winter of year 4.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yun of the inner hall and court gentleman Hu Yuan, who had fought well at Shi'e ravine, were promoted—Yun to vice commissioner of manor houses, Yuan to vice commissioner of rites—in the winter of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，餘黨唐和等復內寇，乃詔湖南安撫、轉運、提點刑獄便宜從事。

translations.literal: Year 5, second month, remnant faction Tang He and others again raided inward—an edict authorized Hunan Pacification, Transport, and Judicial Intendant to act as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year Tang He and other holdouts raided again; Hunan pacification, transport, and judicial officials were told to act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 又特賜官兵土丁錢有差。

translations.literal: Special grants of money were also given to government troops and native levies, with distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Cash grants were also issued to regular troops and native levies according to rank.

sentences.zh: 於是沆檄楊畋等八路入討，覆蕩桃油平、能家源等，皆其巢穴，捕斬首級甚眾。

translations.literal: Kang then ordered Yang Tian and others in eight routes to enter and suppress, overthrowing Taoyouping, Nengjiayuan, and others—all their nests—and capturing and beheading many.
translations.idiomatic: Kang sent Yang Tian and others in eight columns to overrun their nests at Taoyouping and Nengjiayuan and take many heads.

sentences.zh: 詔官兵有功者九百餘人第遷一資，錄其應募討擊者道州進士十四人，並官之。

translations.literal: An edict promoted more than nine hundred meritorious troops one grade and registered fourteen Daozhou jinshi who had answered the call to fight—all were given office.
translations.idiomatic: More than nine hundred soldiers were promoted one step; fourteen Daozhou scholars who had volunteered for the campaign were also given posts.

sentences.zh: 然唐和等猶未平。

translations.literal: Yet Tang He and others were still not pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tang He and his band were still at large.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「如聞賊黨欲降，其罷出兵，逃匿者諭使歸復，州縣拊存之。

translations.literal: Again an edict: "If it is heard the band wish to surrender, halt the troops; those in hiding are to be instructed to return, and prefectures and counties are to comfort and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ran: "If the rebels wish to surrender, halt the armies; tell those in hiding to come home, and let the counties receive them kindly.

sentences.zh: 」是冬，蠻復入寇，與胡元及右侍禁郭正、趙鼎、殿侍王孝先戰於華陰峒隘口，元等死之，劉沆、楊畋皆坐黜。

translations.literal: " That winter the Man again raided inward and fought Hu Yuan, Right Attendant Guo Zheng, Zhao Ding, and Attendant Wang Xiaoxian at the Huayin ravine pass—Yuan and the others died; Liu Kang and Yang Tian were both demoted.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Man raided again. At the Huayin pass they killed Hu Yuan, right attendant Guo Zheng, Zhao Ding, and attendant Wang Xiaoxian; Liu Kang and Yang Tian were demoted.

sentences.zh: 以劉夔代沆為安撫使，夔言：「唐和等既敗官軍，殺將吏，聚眾益自疑，恐浸為邊患，願以詔書招安，就補溪峒首領。

translations.literal: Liu Kui replaced Kang as Pacification Commissioner; Kui said: "Tang He and others, having defeated government troops and killed officers, gather followers and grow more suspicious; I fear they will gradually become a border trouble—I wish to use an edict to recruit and pacify them and appoint stream-cave chiefs on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui replaced Kang as pacification commissioner and argued: "Having beaten our troops and killed officers, Tang He grows bolder and more fearful by the day; he may become a lasting border threat. I ask to offer terms under imperial letter and appoint ravine chiefs on the spot.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 是時，湖湘騷動，兵不得息。

translations.literal: At this time Hunan and Xiang were in turmoil; troops could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and the Xiang region were in turmoil, and the armies had no respite.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，仁宗顧謂輔臣曰：「官軍久戍南方，夏秋之交，瘴癘為虐，其令太醫定方和藥，遣使給之。

translations.literal: Year 6, summer, Renzong turning to his aides said: "Government troops have long garrisoned the south; at the turn of summer and autumn miasma afflicts them—order the Imperial Physicians to fix formulas and compound medicine and dispatch envoys to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth summer Renzong told his ministers: "Our men have long camped in the south; when summer turns to autumn the miasma strikes. Let the imperial physicians prepare remedies and send them out.

sentences.zh: 」自是繼賜緡錢。

translations.literal: " Thereafter cash strings continued to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Cash grants followed as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，夔言敗唐和於銀江源。

translations.literal: Before long Kui reported defeating Tang He at Yinjang source.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kui reported a victory over Tang He at Yinjang source.

sentences.zh: 轉運使周沆亦言指揮辛景賢招降賊黨五十六戶二百五十九人，錄其首領，戒所部拊存之。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Zhou Kang also reported that commander Xin Jingxian had recruited fifty-six households and two hundred fifty-nine persons of the band faction, registered their leaders, and warned subordinates to comfort and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Zhou Kang reported that commander Xin Jingxian had won over fifty-six households and two hundred fifty-nine rebels, enrolled their leaders, and ordered local officials to care for them.

sentences.zh: 先是，命三司戶部判官崔嶧為體量安撫，往議討除、招安二策，既而知桂陽監宋守信奏：「唐和嘯聚千餘眾為盜，五六年卒未能克者，朝廷不許窮討故也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fiscal Judicial Commissioner Cui Yi had been ordered as Investigating Pacifier to discuss the two strategies of extermination and recruitment; then it was learned that Guiyang director Song Shouxin memorialized: "Tang He has rallied more than a thousand as bandits—for five or six years they ultimately could not be conquered because the court would not permit thorough pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier fiscal commissioner Cui Yi had been sent to weigh extermination against negotiation; then Guiyang director Song Shouxin wrote: "Tang He has held more than a thousand men in the hills for five or six years because the court would not let anyone finish the job.

sentences.zh: 今衡州監酒黃士元頗習溪峒事，願得敢戰士二千、引路土丁二百，優給金帛，使之逐捕，必得然後已，並敕亓贇等合力以進。

translations.literal: Now Huang Shiyuan, Hengzhou wine supervisor, knows stream-cave affairs quite well and wishes two thousand fierce fighters and two hundred guide native levies, with rich gold and silk, to pursue and capture them—he must have them before he stops—and Qi Yun and others are also ordered to unite force and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou wine supervisor Huang Shiyuan, who knows the ravines well, asks for two thousand fighters and two hundred native guides, with generous reward, to hunt Tang He to the end, and orders Qi Yun and the rest to press together.

sentences.zh: 彼既勢窮，必將款附。

translations.literal: Once their power is exhausted they will surely come to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once cornered, they will surely submit.

sentences.zh: 」詔用其策，於是大發兵討之。

translations.literal: " An edict adopted his plan; then troops were greatly sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: " The court took his advice and launched a major campaign.

sentences.zh: 其眾果懼，遁入郴州黃莽山，由趙峒轉寇英、韶州，依山自保。

translations.literal: Their host indeed feared, fled into Huangmang Mountain in Chenzhou, by Zhao ravine turned to raid Ying and Shaozhou, and relied on the mountains to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They fled in fear to Huangmang Mountain in Chenzhou, then through Zhao ravine raided Ying and Shaozhou, holding the high ground.

sentences.zh: 是冬，帝閔士卒暴露，復諭執政密戒主帥安恤。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor pitied the troops exposed to the elements and again secretly instructed the council to warn commanders to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor, pitying men camped in the open, privately told his ministers to remind commanders to care for them.

sentences.zh: 七年，唐和遣其子執要領詣官，自言願貸糧米，居所保峒中。

translations.literal: Year 7, Tang He sent his son bearing the required tallies to the officials, stating that he wished to borrow grain and rice and would dwell in the ravine he held.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Tang He sent his son with tallies to the officials, asking for grain on credit and offering to remain in his ravine.

sentences.zh: 時楊畋復為湖南鈐轄，詔趨連、韶州山下，與廣南東、西轉運使共告諭之，使以兵械上官，質其親屬。

translations.literal: Yang Tian was again Hunan Control Commissioner—an edict ordered him to hurry to the foot of Lian and Shaozhou mountains, jointly announce and instruct with the Guangnan east and west transport commissioners, make them turn weapons over to superiors, and take kin as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tian had returned as Hunan control commissioner; he was sent to the foot of Lian and Shaozhou with the Guangnan transport commissioners to announce terms—surrender arms and leave kin as hostages.

sentences.zh: 詔補唐和、盤知諒、房承映、承泰、文運等五人為峒主，授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼監察御史、武騎尉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Tang He, Pan Zhiliang, Fang Chengying, Chengtai, Wenyun, and five others as ravine lords, granting Silver Radiance Grand Master, Honorary Libationer of the Imperial Academy with concurrent Investigating Censor, and Martial Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He, Pan Zhiliang, Fang Chengying, Fang Chengtai, Wenyun, and others—five men in all—were made ravine lords with the titles silver radiance grand master, honorary imperial-academy libationer and investigating censor, and martial cavalry captain.

sentences.zh: 知諒等，蓋唐和黨也。

translations.literal: Zhiliang and the others were Tang He's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiliang and the rest were Tang He's men.

sentences.zh: 至冬，其眾悉降。

translations.literal: By winter their host had all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By winter they had all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年，邵州蠻舒光銀因湖南安撫司官自陳捍禦之勞，願於峒中置中勝州，詔可。

translations.literal: Huangyou year 5, Shaozhou Man Shu Guangyin, through Hunan Pacification officials, stated his merit in defense and wished to establish Zhongsheng Prefecture in his ravine—an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangyou Shaozhou Man Shu Guangyin, through pacification officials, claimed credit for defense and asked to establish Zhongsheng Prefecture in his ravine—the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，羅城峒蠻寇澧州，發兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Jiayou year 2, Luocheng ravine Man raided Lizhou—troops were sent and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiayou Luocheng ravine Man raided Lizhou; troops drove them back.

sentences.zh: 三年，以施州蠻向永勝所領州為安定州。

translations.literal: Year 3, the prefecture led by Shizhou Man Xiang Yongsheng was made Anding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the domain of Shizhou Man Xiang Yongsheng was made Anding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，以邵州蠻楊光倩知徽州。

translations.literal: Year 5, Shaozhou Man Yang Guangqian was made Administrator of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Shaozhou Man Yang Guangqian was appointed prefect of Hui.

sentences.zh: 光倩，通漢之子也。

translations.literal: Guangqian was Tonghan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqian was the son of Tonghan.

sentences.zh: 通漢，慶曆初嘗入貢，既死，光倩襲之。

translations.literal: Tonghan in early Qingli had come to offer tribute; after he died Guangqian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghan had presented tribute early in Qingli; when he died Guangqian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 舊制，溪峒知州卒，承襲者許進奉行州事，撫遏蠻人，及五年，安撫司為奏給敕告。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when a stream-cave Administrator died the successor might advance and conduct prefectural affairs, pacify and restrain Man, and after five years the Pacification Commission would memorialize to grant the patent.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a ravine prefect died his heir might govern provisionally, keep the Man quiet, and after five years the pacification office would memorialize for an imperial patent.

sentences.zh: 至是，光倩行州事七年，無他過，故命之。

translations.literal: At this Guangqian had conducted prefectural affairs for seven years without other fault—therefore he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqian had governed for seven years without fault, and so received formal appointment.
